model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", spans from 0 to 65 percent. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circular markers, starting at approximately 0% ACC at 10¹ and declining to around 20% at 10³. The "FT" method, shown as a blue line with triangular markers, begins near 30% ACC at 10¹ and decreases to about 10% at 10³. The "IKE" method, depicted with red lines and triangle markers, starts at approximately 35% ACC at 10¹ and falls to roughly 20% at 10³. The "MEND" method, indicated by a brown line with square markers, begins at about 35% ACC at 10¹ and declines to around 25% at 10³. The "MEMIT" method, shown with a purple line and diamond markers, starts near 35% ACC at 10¹ and decreases to approximately 25% at 10³. The "ROME" method, represented by a green line with square markers, begins at roughly 45% ACC at 10¹ and decreases to about 35% ACC at 10³. All lines show a general downward trend as the co-occurrence number increases.
